conviction_note: Small net-positive evidence (credit tracking ~45-50bp better YoY in the company's own monthly 8-Ks, a consensus of $5.45-5.50 that sits below Q2's $5.81 despite a guided NIM catch-up) is offset by a name whose last three prints all closed lower (including after a +24% Q2 beat, -2.36%), a card peer (Synchrony) that beat and slipped this morning, and a run of pre-print target cuts flagging expenses/marketing; p_up 52 on an abs move of 4.5 (option-implied 4.45) gives +0.18, while the findings sum to +0.15 - the two agree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus $5.45 (Nasdaq/Zacks) to $5.50 (MarketBeat, GuruFocus, Investing.com); revenue ~$16.25bn. Two agreeing source families: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/countdown-capital-one-cof-q3-121520570.html , https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-20-capital-one-financial-co-stock/ , https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/jpmorgan-cuts-target-for-capital-one-stock-to-usd-227-00/70337728 (cites both $5.50 MarketBeat and $5.45 Nasdaq, revenue $16.25bn vs $15.46bn a year earlier). No company guidance on EPS; management gives qualitative guidance only (NIM catch-up, H2 marketing higher, synergies on track). print_vs_bar_pct is measured against $5.475 adjusted EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest ~1.9% of float, ~2.2-2.3 days to cover (equibles snapshot, undated, ~July 2026, https://equibles.com/stocks/COF ); FINRA settlement 2026-04-30: 8,223,331 shares short, 1.92 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/cof/shortinterest , https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/cof/short-interest ). No September/October settlement found. Not a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d +0.84 vol points (mild put bid, 'balanced'), put/call OI 0.76, event-implied move 4.45% (straddle 4.71%), Bloomberg-cited implied ~4.6%. Stock 201.57, -21.85% from 52w high, +0.51% over 20d, +1.77% over 5d. Sell-side has been cutting targets into the print (JPM 246->227 on 10-15, TD Cowen 253->242, Barclays 240->237, Evercore 230->220, Citi 295->280, MS 273->267) without rating changes.

findings.finding: Capital One's own monthly 8-Ks put Domestic Card net charge-offs at 4.12% in July and 4.16% in August 2026 (June 4.37%), against a Q3 2025 domestic card NCO rate of 4.63%: two of three Q3 months tracking ~45-50bp better YoY and ~20bp better than June, on ~$257bn of average card loans (~$300m/quarter less NCO vs a year ago at that run-rate). 30+ delinquency rose seasonally 3.39% -> 3.48% -> 3.57% (Jun-Aug), below the 3.89% of Sept 30 2025; management at Barclays (09-16) said delinquencies are in line with seasonality and charge-offs better than seasonal, helped by high recoveries. September's month is not yet public (COF files the quarter-end month with the release).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has been improving all year and the stock fell after Q1 (-1.52%) and Q2 (-2.36%) prints that both showed falling NCOs and a reserve release ($662m in Q2); improving credit has not been paid for on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the monthly metrics are wire-carried (Newsquawk headline) and consensus moved only ~+0.2% in 30 days. What is not fully in consensus is the allowance consequence: with Q3 NCO ~50bp below last year and DQs below last year, a further reserve release or a smaller-than-modelled seasonal build is possible; if the market had priced that, consensus would sit at or above Q2's $5.81 rather than $5.45-5.50.
findings.independence: July 8-K (4.12% / 3.48%) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927628/000092762826000093/ex991july2026creditmetrics.htm and June 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000927628/000092762826000084/ex991june2026creditmetrics.htm are the same company series; Q3 2025 comparator from the 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927628/000092762825000276/cof-20250930.htm ; management commentary https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/capital-one-at-barclays-conference-growth-bets-stay-on-track-93CH-4904188 (company, not independent).

findings.finding: Consensus Q3 adjusted EPS of $5.45-5.50 sits ~6% below Q2's $5.81 even though management guided on the Q2 call to a Q3 NIM catch-up (average cash aligning to lower ending cash) plus an extra day worth ~9bp, and Q3 card NCOs are tracking lower than Q2; the offsets the Street is modelling are seasonally higher H2 marketing and no repeat of Q2's $662m reserve release (~$0.80/share after tax). Q2's consensus was $4.68 and the print $5.81 (+24%), showing the post-Discover model is hard for the Street to track.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: +24% adjusted EPS beat, stock +0.34% after hours then -2.36% over the window; Q1 2026 -1.52%; Q4 2025 print -7.56%. Three straight negative print reactions, the latest after a large beat.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a repeat of Q2's run-rate, consensus would be near $5.8 and the stock would not be trading at ~8.7x that run-rate annualised with targets being cut; the bar is set ~$0.30 under Q2. The beat is likely partly expected (whisper) and this name has not rewarded beats, so the reaction share of a beat is small.
findings.independence: Consensus sources: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/countdown-capital-one-cof-q3-121520570.html ; the NIM-catch-up guidance is also in https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/capital-one-financial-corporation-q2-123000125.html (same call, not independent). Shares the credit fact with finding 1 only in that lower NCO helps both; the EPS gap is sized here net of that.

findings.finding: Expense/marketing ramp risk for the guide: on the Q2 call management said marketing trends higher in H2 (Q2 marketing ~$1.7bn, +23% YoY) and Brex marketing would ramp 'later in the year'; at Barclays (09-16) the finance SVP said fixing the Discover 'brownout' and growth 'will likely require more marketing spend', with ~2/3 of the $2.5bn opex synergies still to come by H2 2027. Into the print six brokers cut targets (JPM -$19 to $227, TD Cowen, Barclays, Evercore, Citi on cost of equity, MS) and Nasdaq's preview flags higher expenses and weaker deposit trends.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2: non-interest expense +7% q/q with marketing +11% accompanied a beat that the stock sold (-2.36%); AmEx's Q2 2026 beat was also sold (~-6.5%) on 12% expense growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced (target cuts, -22% from high). What is not priced is the 2027 marketing/expense trajectory, which management only gives on the call; if the market had fully priced a heavier 2027 spend, targets would already have reset rather than trickling down through October.
findings.independence: Target-cut roundup https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/jpmorgan-cuts-target-for-capital-one-stock-to-usd-227-00/70337728 (different source, same direction); Q2 marketing figures https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-capital-one-beats-q2-2026-profit-estimates-as-stock-edges-higher-93CH-4804418 (company); AmEx Q2 reaction https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/american-express-q2-profit-rises-8-percent-tops-forecasts-despite-higher-expense-07242026 .

findings.finding: Card peer read from this morning (2026-10-20, bmo): Synchrony beat Q3 ($2.68 vs $2.42 consensus), NCO 4.79% vs 5.16% a year ago, 30+ DQ 4.34% steady, FY26 EPS raised to ~$9.50 (top of range), yet shares fell ~2.3% premarket on rising costs (other expense +10%) and funding pressure: card-credit improvement is being sold on expenses this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: COF's own last two prints were sold despite better credit (-1.52%, -2.36%), the same pattern SYF shows today.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed this morning, after every COF preview and target change was written; COF was +1.77% over five days into the print with a flat 20d run-up, which does not look like a stock that has marked down for a sector 'beat and sell' pattern. Partly priced intraday today.
findings.independence: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-synchrony-beats-q3-2026-estimates-but-shares-slip-93CH-4960206 (same event, different write-up). Peer proxy, not COF's own number.

findings.finding: Peer credit read: JPMorgan's Q3 2026 Card Services net charge-off rate reported at 2.91% vs 3.15% in 3Q25 and 3.34% in 2Q26, with the ~3.2% full-year card NCO guide held (Q2 10-Q shows the guide cut from ~3.4% to ~3.2%): prime card credit improving through Q3, consistent with COF's July/August trend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as finding 1 (credit); COF has not been paid for credit improvement on the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; JPM reported a week ago. Its use is as a cross-check that COF's September (unreported) month did not break the trend.
findings.independence: Single secondary source for the 2.91%; guide in JPM Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026054343/jpm-20260630.htm . Proxy; overlaps conceptually with finding 1 and is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: September datapoint ahead of COF's own: the Capital One Master Trust 10-D for the September 2026 monthly period (filed 2026-10-15) shows an annualized net default rate of 1.69% (July period ~1.80%, May ~2.23%) and 60+ day delinquency 1.22% (July ~1.16%): the seasoned securitised pool stayed stable into quarter-end, a small read that September card NCO did not spike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of the stock trading on trust data.
findings.why_not_priced: Trust 10-Ds are not wire-carried and the September company 8-K comes only with the release; the trust is a seasoned prime subset (net default ~1.7% vs ~4.2% for the domestic card book), so it is a narrow proxy for the whole book and is sized accordingly.
findings.independence: Prior trust readings from company-hosted servicer documents (search snippets, ir-capitalone.gcs-web.com); same issuer family. Narrow proxy, sized below the company monthly series in finding 1.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity: Q2 buybacks were $2.7bn (~14m shares; $5.2bn YTD) with ~$9bn of authorization left, CET1 13.7% against an 11% long-term need and a 9.0% SCB-based requirement frozen through Sept 2027; with the stock ~22% below its 52-week high, the Q3 repurchase pace and any acceleration commentary is a support line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $2.7bn buyback came with a -2.36% reaction; capital return has not been a positive catalyst on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public; the unpriced part is pace, since the CFO said the 11% is 'not a target' and they are 'not rushing'. If the market expected acceleration at these prices, the stock would not be lagging the average target by 20%+.
findings.independence: SCB freeze in the Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000927628/000092762826000089/cof-20260630.htm and https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2635353/capital-one-announces-stress-test-results (company documents).

findings.finding: Integration guidance reaffirmed qualitatively at Barclays (09-16): earnings power 'strikingly sort of right around the same level' as originally expected for Discover, credit originations moved onto COF's platform at the start of September, back-book migration waves July/October/January, Discover brownout expected to start reversing in H2, Brex 'promising green shoots'; domestic card period-end loans rose from $259.0bn (June 30) to $260.6bn (Aug 31).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Integration milestones have not moved the stock on print days in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (public conference); the margin of new information is whether Q3 shows the brownout's shrinkage stabilising, which the August loan balance hints at.
findings.independence: Loan balances from the August 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927628/000092762826000132/ex991august2026creditmetri.htm (company). Shares the Barclays source with finding 3 but a different line (loan growth vs expense).

findings.finding: Insider sale: the retail-bank president (Celia Karam) sold ~$377k of stock on 2026-10-15, five days before the print; small and likely routine.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4; trivially small against a ~$125bn market cap. Filed for completeness.

baseline_tension: Evidence is near-balanced, matching the balanced lean and the mild +0.84 put skew; the positive credit/consensus facts are public and the reaction history (three straight negative print reactions, including after a 24% beat) cuts against paying for them.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): COF sold a +24% beat (-2.36%) and fell after Q1 too; credit finding 0.4 -> 0.3 and consensus-gap finding 0.5 -> 0.3; p_up 53 -> 52 (expected_move 0.27 -> 0.18).
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy below the broad series): trust 10-D finding 0.15 -> 0.1, below the company monthly series; JPM peer read 0.2 -> 0.1 as a single-secondary-source proxy that overlaps finding 1.
Lesson 6 (bar): bar sourced to two agreeing estimate families ($5.45/$5.50), no cap needed; all findings resolve inside the window, post-window catalysts are in outside_window.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest ~2% of float / ~2 days, not crowded; negatives left at size; skew mild so no sign-vs-skew adjustment.
